update.title: OT-98.2: the 30 verses closed as data, read outward and woven (#2160)
update.strand: open threads on completed clusters (#2160), OT-98.2 (M18 x M72)
update.researcher_instruction: "OT-98.2: weave as proposed in section 2; add 1Sa 25 and 2Ki 18-19 / Isa 36-37 as verse items for later strands; then close OT-98.2 and OT-98.10." (2026-10-19)
update.method: The 30 verses of the 182 M18 x M72 verses that the M18 strand closed as data or route C (under the M72 scope ruling later called premature, #2160 v7) read outward by guide v2 (#2168), each in its passage, with 1Ki 2:13-25. 23 carry the inner being, with about a dozen uncited neighbours; 2 parallels; Mat 18:23 carried by its parable; 4 data with reasons (2Ch 36:10, Dan 11:8, 1Ki 5:17, Judg 1:35). Placed by appending to the end of the named sections in 16 chapters.
update.claims_changed_note: 27 new claims, one per new passage that goes beyond its verses.
update.not_woven_note: 1Sa 25 (Nabal and Abigail) and 2Ki 18-19 / Isa 36-37 (the Assyrian speech) added as verse items on OT-98 for later strands. Data: 2Ch 36:10, Dan 11:8, 1Ki 5:17, Judg 1:35 (the hand as power, noted for signpost #1893).

new.text: Under rulers who make injustice law, the psalmist's thought of falling was met by steadfast love before the question was asked
new.beyond_text: reads the order of Psa 94:18-22 around the question

new.text: Trust in God can be attacked by casting doubt on the one who leads and by naming a past of power
new.beyond_text: reads the speech's aim as the people's trust

new.text: Rule can be turned into injustice, and power can be given for a time and used at will
new.beyond_text: sets Psa 94:20 beside Rev 11:6 as two sides of authority

new.text: God's call can go unanswered, and the same passage sets beside it the servant's ear awakened morning by morning
new.beyond_text: joins Isa 50:2 and 50:4 in one passage

new.text: Absalom's burning of Joab's field was a demand to be seen by his father
new.beyond_text: reads the fire through Absalom's own words

new.text: The one who holds power holds life for those under it, and in Jesus' parable the king uses it to release out of pity
new.beyond_text: joins the king's wrath and favour (Pro 16:14-15) with the parable's release (Mat 18:27)

new.text: Loyalty can fail at its post: Abner did not keep watch over the Lord's anointed, while David refused to strike him
new.beyond_text: sets Abner's failure beside David's restraint

new.text: Joab yielded the honour of taking Rabbah to David
new.beyond_text: reads Joab's message as yielding the honour

new.text: Solomon on his throne showed honour upward to his mother, then refused her request
new.beyond_text: sets the honour beside the refusal

new.text: A gift can be judged and resented between friends
new.beyond_text: reads Hiram's words as resentment of the gift

new.text: Anger can rise at contempt for a request that rested on good done
new.beyond_text: joins the request's ground (25:7-8) to Nabal's contempt and David's anger

new.text: Anger can rest on a misreading and still decide, and it abates when its object is gone
new.beyond_text: reads the king's charge as a misreading of Haman's plea

new.text: Fear can come with seeing what has been decided against oneself
new.beyond_text: names Haman's seeing as the ground of his begging

new.text: Coveting can add until it leaves the coveter alone
new.beyond_text: reads 'made to dwell alone' as the end of the adding

new.text: Adonijah's wish for Abishag was read by Solomon as the throne asked for again; the verses give Solomon's reading, not Adonijah's heart
new.beyond_text: separates Solomon's reading from Adonijah's unstated intent

new.text: Solomon's desire to build was carried out by the forced labour of the peoples left in the land
new.beyond_text: joins 'all that Solomon desired to build' to the forced labour

new.text: Joseph's counsel plans against a famine he has been shown
new.beyond_text: reads the counsel as planning ahead from what was shown

new.text: Daniel's visions picture the will made absolute: doing as one pleases and becoming great, even against the Prince of the host
new.beyond_text: reads the vision's figures as the same will

new.text: The king's remembering of Vashti was turned aside by a pleasure offered, and the young women's own wishes were not asked
new.beyond_text: reads the servants' proposal as redirecting the remembering

new.text: At the king's feast every guest was set free to do as he desired before the merry heart gave its command
new.beyond_text: sets Est 1:8 before Est 1:10

new.text: A wrong expectation can be what a teaching answers
new.beyond_text: reads Luk 19:11 as the parable's occasion

new.text: A promise not to refuse can be overridden by an oath
new.beyond_text: sets the promise beside the oath

new.text: The heart is called on as the witness of the harm it knows it did
new.beyond_text: reads 'You know in your own heart' as the heart as witness

new.text: Life is said to flow from another's face and favour
new.beyond_text: reads Pro 16:15 as a source of life

new.text: Barzillai asks to die in his own city near his parents' grave and gives his place at court to another
new.beyond_text: reads the offer of Chimham as giving his place

new.text: God names his heart and eyes as set on a place
new.beyond_text: reads 1Ki 9:3 as God's heart named with the house

new.text: God's power is put as a question to a people who did not answer him
new.beyond_text: reads the questions of Isa 50:2 as addressed to the people's silence

tellings.passage: Under rulers who make injustice into law
Trust in God can be attacked from outside
Rule can be turned into injustice
God's own call can go unanswered
Absalom gave the reason for the burned field
The one who holds power holds life for those under it
Loyalty can fail at its post
Honour can be yielded
Honour can be shown upward by the one on the throne
A gift can be judged and resented between friends
Anger can rise at contempt for a request
Anger can rest on a misreading and still decide
Fear can come with seeing what has been decided
Coveting can add until it leaves the coveter alone
Wanting a person can be read as wanting something else
A king's desire can be carried out by other people's labour
Joseph's counsel to Pharaoh plans against a famine
The visions picture the same will
What others do with a king's remembering
Before the king's merry heart gave its command
A wrong expectation can be what a teaching answers
A promise can be given and then overridden by an oath
Solomon calls on Shimei's own heart as the witness
Life is also said to flow from another's face
Barzillai, at eighty, asks to go home to die
God names his heart with a place
His power is also his question to a people who did not answer him
